text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry for your loss. Thank you for reaching out. Before we look at options, I'd like to hear from A and B too, so we are working with everyone's concerns, not just one side. Could you tell me a bit more: what do you think the house is worth, what share of it did your dad leave to each of you, and what would you like to see happen?

Thanks. I don’t know the house’s value or what shares Dad’s will gives us, so I won’t guess. I want a fair financial share and won’t subsidize A buying it at a discount. I’d like us to hear from everyone and work it out; there’s no rush.

Hello, I'm helping you and your sisters talk through what happens with the house your dad left. C has told me she has concerns about the idea of you and your husband buying it at a "family discount". I'd like to hear your side. What are you hoping for, and what matters most to you?
I’m hoping my husband and I can buy the house at a family discount. What matters most to me is being financially independent. I know C hasn’t agreed, and I can’t proceed without her agreement.

Hello, I'm helping you and your sisters work out what happens with the house your dad left in his will. I've heard from C so far, and I'd like to hear from you too. What would you like to see happen, and what do you need? C mentioned money might be important for you.
I’d be grateful if we could find a way for me to get money from my share, so I can start a dance studio. I’m not sure what’s fair or what the arrangements would be yet.

Thank you all for your replies. Here's what I propose as a first step, and I want to hear objections from each of you before we commit to anything.

First, find the will and check what share of the house each of you has, and who is handling the estate. Second, get one independent professional valuation of the house, split between the three of you. That gives everyone the same facts.

Once we know the value, A can make an offer. C has said she won't accept a discount that quietly takes money from her or B's shares, and B needs cash for her dance studio. A possible middle ground: A buys at full market value, or at a discount only if you three all agree on it openly, with B's needs covered from the proceeds. You can also take time; C mentioned there is no rush.

Do any of you object to starting with the will and a shared valuation?
No objection to checking the will and getting a shared valuation. I’m not agreeing to any purchase or discount yet.

Thank you for your honest reply. I want to check a concern with you: a discount on the house would reduce what C and B receive, and C has already said she won't agree to that. Would you be open to buying at an independently valued market price, or at most a discount that C and B both agree to openly? I've proposed to all three of you that we start by finding the will and getting one shared professional valuation, split between you. Does that work for you?
Yes, I’m willing to find the will and share the cost of one professional valuation. I’d discuss any discount openly with B and C, but I’m not agreeing to a price before we know more.

Thank you for telling me about the dance studio. A concern I'd like to check with you: your share of the house is money the three of you need to divide fairly, and C has said she won't accept A buying it at a discount that reduces her share. Your needs matter just as much as theirs. I've suggested to all three of you that we start by finding the will and getting one shared professional valuation of the house. Then A can buy at a fair price and your share of the proceeds could help fund the studio. Does that sound fair to you?
That sounds like a sensible way to start, as long as the valuation and everyone’s share are worked out fairly. I’d hope my proceeds could go toward the studio.

Good news: all three of you agree on the first step. You will find the will and see what share of the house each sister has, and you three will split the cost of one independent professional valuation. Nothing about a sale, price, or discount is agreed yet, so C's position is respected. Next steps: one of you locates the will and the executor, then you book a valuer. Once we have the value, we can talk about whether A buys the house and how B's share helps fund the studio. Please let me know when you have the will's details or the valuation.
Okay. I’ll help coordinate finding the will and executor, but nothing beyond that is agreed.

Thank you for agreeing to the shared valuation and being open about any discount. That helps a lot. Next step is locating the will and the executor to confirm what share each sister has, then booking one professional valuation split between the three of you. Once we have a market value, we can discuss your offer, and any discount would be discussed openly with C and B. Please keep me posted.
I’ll keep you posted once we’ve located the will and executor.

Thank you for your reply. The three of you have now agreed to find the will and share the cost of one professional valuation. Once we know the market value and each sister's share, we can work out how your share of the proceeds could help fund the dance studio, and whether A buys the house at a price all of you accept. Please let me know if anything about the plan doesn't feel fair to you.
Nothing feels unfair about that plan so far. I’d just like us to keep in view that I’m hoping to use my share to start the studio.

Thank you for coordinating the will and executor. I'll keep a shared note of everyone's concerns so nothing is forgotten: A wants to buy the house and values financial independence; you want a fair share and no subsidy of a discounted sale; B wants her share to help fund a dance studio. All three of you have agreed on locating the will and splitting one professional valuation. No price, discount, or sale is agreed. I'll wait to hear from A about the will and executor, and we'll take it from there.
That works. I’ll wait for the will and executor details before we arrange the valuation.

Understood, and I'll keep your studio goal in view as part of the plan. I've noted it alongside the others' concerns so it isn't lost. The current agreed step is locating the will and getting one shared valuation. Once A reports back on the will and executor, and we have a valuation, we can discuss how your share of the proceeds supports the studio. Nothing unfair to you has been agreed, and you can object at any point.
Thank you. That sounds fine for now; I’d appreciate keeping the studio in mind when we discuss the proceeds.
